title: Investigate customer-reported overage: rate-limit retry causing double-counted usage
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customer ACME reported an unexpected ~28% overage on their monthly bill for February. Support opened ticket SUP-9872 after the customer noticed token counts that don't match their internal instrumentation. Initial support triage found two anomalies: a burst of 429s returned to the client on 2025-02-12 02:14 UTC and a delayed metering aggregation job that reprocessed an ingestion window for the same account on 2025-02-13 04:00 UTC. This ticket tracks the engineering investigation to reconcile usage, determine root cause, and coordinate credits and product fixes.
steps_to_reproduce: Simulate client with aggressive retry policy (exponential backoff with jitter) hitting per-minute rate-limits; confirm duplicate requests from retries are being accepted by downstream due to transient 429 handling
Replay ingestion pipeline for a 24h window with synthetic duplicate events to observe aggregation behavior in usage-aggregator v1.7
Force a delayed aggregation job (kill metering-worker then restart) to reproduce double-processing within the dedupe window
investigation_notes: 2025-02-20 14:10 - Marco: Pulled raw events for ACME account for 2025-02-12..2025-02-14 from Kafka topic 'usage-raw-v2'; observed ~12k duplicate request IDs in a 6 minute burst starting 02:14:05 UTC.

2025-02-21 09:22 - Aisha: Checked rate-limiter logs; upstream service returned 429 and client retried immediately. Client SDK version 2.3.1 retries up to 5 times with no server-advised 'Retry-After' handling for our 429 responses. Reproduced with sandbox client that retries aggressively.

2025-02-22 11:02 - Marco: Found metering-aggregator job re-run on 2025-02-13 04:00 UTC due to scheduled maintenance + missed heartbeat; when reprocessing the window it didn't respect event-level idempotency for events older than 2 minutes, causing duplicates to be counted again.
2025-02-24 16:35 - Ops: Disk pressure in cluster metering-prod-3 caused job restart; upgrade to node image rolled back and requeued the aggregation job.
findings: Primary cause: combination of client-side aggressive retries generating duplicate requests and metering-aggregator reprocessing without strict idempotency/dedupe across replays.
Secondary cause: Rate-limiter did not include a machine-readable Retry-After header in 429 responses for per-minute limits, leading client SDKs to retry too quickly.
Observation: Our usage events include a client_request_id but dedupe in aggregator only dedupes within a 2-minute sliding window; late replays >2 minutes can lead to double-counting.

Scope: Preliminary audit shows ~28% of ACME's billed tokens for that day came from reprocessed duplicates. No evidence of malicious activity. Similar pattern found for 3 other mid-market customers with aggressive retry patterns.
action_items: Short-term mitigation (P0): Issue immediate one-time credit to ACME for the confirmed overage period and root-cause communication via SUPPORT-ACCT-EMAIL; credit amount proposed $3,200 (approved by finance pending final reconciliation).
Patch: Update metering-aggregator to use a 24-hour idempotency window keyed on client_request_id + model+account; ensure replay-safe behavior. Target: deploy patch in release metering-2025.03.
Rate-limit header change: Emit 'Retry-After' (seconds) and 'X-RateLimit-Reset' timestamps in 429 responses for minute and burst enforcement so compliant SDKs back off correctly.
SDK guidance: Publish a best-practices doc for retry behavior and update official SDKs to honor server Retry-After and implement jittered exponential backoff defaults.
Monitoring: Add alert when metering-aggregator restarts cause reprocessing of windows older than 15 minutes; create SLO for metering-latency (median ingestion -> aggregation <5m).
Testing: Add end-to-end test that replays delayed events >10 minutes and validates no double-counting occurs.
linked_prs: github.com/redwood-inference/metering/pull/842 - aggregator: increase dedupe window and add replay idempotency
github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/2011 - gateway: include Retry-After header for rate-limit responses
github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/456 - sdk: honor Retry-After and reduce default retry aggressiveness
customer_communications: 2025-02-20 17:05 - Support: Acknowledged customer's report and escalated to engineering; asked for 48h for full reconciliation.
2025-02-24 09:30 - Support: Confirmed provisional findings and offered a temporary credit; awaiting finance sign-off for formal credit transaction.
2025-02-28 12:00 - Engineering -> ACME: Provided detailed root-cause summary, planned fixes, and timeline for patch release. Offered contact for follow-up audit of future invoices.
resolution: Work in progress: patch PRs opened and under review. Provisional credit approved by finance for ACME; formal charge-back scheduled for 2025-03-02 pending final reconciliation. Long-term fixes scoped and scheduled for metering-2025.03 release.
root_cause: Delayed metering-aggregator replay combined with duplicate requests from client retry behavior. Lack of server 'Retry-After' header and too-short dedupe window allowed duplicates to be counted twice during a reprocessing event.
next_steps: Merge and deploy PRs: meter-842 and platform-2011 (owner: Marco).
Coordinate with Support to issue final invoice adjustment and post the credit on 2025-03-02.
Add monitoring and e2e tests before GA of metering-2025.03 release.
Product: draft SDK retry best-practices doc and circulate to major customers by 2025-03-10.
